audit.why: Singed on every stage except level 6 already agrees with the mirror at audits/top/malphite__singed.json, which concluded that level 6 is the only Malphite row. The one thing out of place is the difficulty number: 3/10 for Malphite's side on his page inverts to a very easy lane here, not the 7/10 currently shown on a 58.85% matchup labelled FAV with the favoured tone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike is described as a stage you retreat from, and Unstoppable Force's cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100. Once you know it is a dash you do not have to retreat from it at all, and one denial costs him over two minutes at rank 1. Turning the page's single 'back off' stage into an aggression window is the largest available upgrade to this matchup.
audit.corrected: Unstoppable Force 130/115/100, and it is deniable rather than something to hide from.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions are absent. (a) Unstoppable Force is a dash and Mega Adhesive grounds — a Malphite standing in the goo cannot cast his ultimate. The page instead says to back off whenever it is up. (b) Granite Shield recharges only after he goes a few seconds without being hit; a continuous Poison Trail never lets that timer start.
audit.why: Riot Mega Adhesive: 'slowing and grounding enemies who walk on it.' Riot Unstoppable Force: 'Malphite launches himself to a location at high speed' — dash flag on the kit. Riot Granite Shield: 'Malphite is shielded by a layer of rock which absorbs damage up to 10% of his maximum Health. If Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds, this effect recharges.' Poison Trail is a continuous tick, so it is a permanent shield-denial tool and nothing on the page says so. The mirror reaches the same conclusion about the ultimate from Malphite's side and calls it the most important interaction in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Glue him and the ult does not fire; keep poison on him and Granite Shield never comes back.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit file's derived flags put 'grounding' on Seismic Shard (Q) and Ground Slam (E). Riot's own text for those two describes a move-speed steal and an attack-speed reduction respectively, with no grounding.
audit.why: Flag misfire from tooltip parsing. Recording it so nobody later writes 'Malphite grounds you' onto a page — I asserted nothing from it.

edits.before: He stacks armor — your poison is magic. Proxy through him, fling his Q-slow, and never let him sit on a full Unstoppable Force cycle.
edits.after: He stacks armour — your poison is magic, and it also stops Granite Shield recharging. Goo grounds Unstoppable Force clean off.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force is un-dodgeable and one-shots a low-HP Singed — back off when his R is up and reassert only after it is burned or your first item is complete.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is a dash and Mega Adhesive grounds — a Malphite standing in your goo cannot cast it at all. Glue him as he winds up instead of backing off the wave.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force is the one moment Malphite is genuinely dangerous — it is un-dodgeable and one-shots a Singed who sits low; back off when his R is up and farm until it is burned or you have your first item.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force one-shots a Singed who sits low, but it is a dash and Mega Adhesive grounds — goo under his feet stops the cast outright, and at 130s a single denial buys you the whole wave cycle.

edits.before: Track Unstoppable Force before every commit and back off when his R is available
edits.after: Track Unstoppable Force, 130s at rank 1, and glue him — grounded he cannot cast it

edits.before: Malphite's entire identity is stacking armor to win the auto-trade, and your Poison Trail is magic damage — his armor does nothing. Run straight through him on wave one and let the cloud tick while he Q-slows you into it. When he steps up to last-hit, drop Mega Adhesive in his path and Fling him backward; a slow, dash-less tank rooted in goo and launched into your poison is three seconds of free damage he cannot answer. Stay near your side of the lane so he must walk into your range, and never sit low when Unstoppable Force is available — that is his only genuine threat window in the early lane.
edits.after: Malphite's entire identity is stacking armor to win the auto-trade, and your Poison Trail is magic damage — his armor does nothing. It does something better as well: Granite Shield only recharges after he goes a few seconds untouched, and a poison cloud sitting on him never lets that clock start. When he steps up to last-hit, drop Mega Adhesive in his path and Fling him backward; a dash-less tank rooted in goo and launched into your poison is three seconds of free damage he cannot answer. Stay near your side so he must walk into range — and remember the goo grounds, so Unstoppable Force will not fire out of it.

edits.before: The proxy game starts in earnest at Level 4. Walk behind his tower, drop Poison Trail on his returning minions, and let him choose between losing the wave or walking into your cloud to contest it — he cannot chase you through poison without taking the full damage, and his Q slow only helps you by sending him further into your trail. At Level 6 he gets Unstoppable Force, which is un-dodgeable and has enough burst to delete a low-HP Singed in one go; back away, burn Insanity Potion if you have to, and reassert the proxy once his R is on cooldown. First item is your true spike — Rylai's makes your Poison Trail a permanent slow that stacks on top of his Q, and at that point he literally cannot walk away from your cloud.
edits.after: The proxy game starts in earnest at Level 4. Walk behind his tower, drop Poison Trail on his returning minions, and let him choose between losing the wave or walking into your cloud to contest it — he cannot chase you through poison without taking the full damage, and his Q slow only helps you by sending him further into your trail. At Level 6 Unstoppable Force can delete a low-HP Singed in one go, but it is a dash on 130s at rank 1 and grounding turns it off, so the answer is Mega Adhesive under him, not a retreat. First item is your true spike — Rylai's makes Poison Trail a permanent slow stacking on top of his Q, and he cannot walk away from your cloud.
